key_insight: A high-throughput DFT search identified 58 CuI-based ternary compounds with promising p-type transparent conductor behavior, revealing new halide design rules beyond classic oxide delafossites.
engineering_relevance: The study expands the materials palette for transparent electrodes and tandem photovoltaics by pointing to stable, optically transparent, low-hole-mass candidates that can support p-type conductivity.
method: Minima hopping structure search over X–Cu–I ternaries
Density functional theory screening for thermodynamic stability and optical transparency
Selection by light hole effective mass and p-type degeneracy criteria
evidence_signal: From the abstract, 58 candidates were found, including 49 previously unreported compounds and 20 degenerate semiconductors; Cu2FI2 is highlighted with a 3.75 eV gap and 0.262 m0 hole effective mass.
watch_item: These are computational predictions, so experimental synthesis, phase stability under real conditions, and achievable carrier concentrations still need validation.
paper_title: High-throughput computational discovery of CuI-based ternary $p$-type transparent conductors
